### Factual Comparison

#### Defensive Player of the Year (DPOY)
* **Michael Jordan:** Won the award **1 time** (1987–88) [[jordan_accolades_240], [T1]].
* **LeBron James:** Won the award **0 times** [[T2]].

---

#### All-Defensive Team Selections
* **Michael Jordan:**
  * **All-Defensive First Team:** **9 selections** (1987–88, 1988–89, 1989–90, 1990–91, 1991–92, 1992–93, 1995–96, 1996–97, 1997–98) [[jordan_accolades_240], [T1]].
  * **All-Defensive Second Team:** **0 selections** [[T1]].
  * **Total All-Defensive Selections:** **9** [[T1]].

* **LeBron James:**
  * **All-Defensive First Team:** **5 selections** (2008–09, 2009–10, 2010–11, 2011–12, 2012–13) [[lebron_accolades_320], [T2]].
  * **All-Defensive Second Team:** **1 selection** (2013–14) [[lebron_accolades_320], [T2]].
  * **Total All-Defensive Selections:** **6** [[T2]].

---

### Tradeoffs and Analytical Context

* **Accolade Volume & Peak Honors:** By award totals, Michael Jordan holds an advantage in both top-tier defensive honors (9 First Team selections to LeBron's 5) and peak individual defensive recognition, having secured a Defensive Player of the Year award [[jordan_accolades_240], [T1], [T2]].
* **Analytical Impact vs. Accolades (Subjective/Contextual Nuance):**
  * The evidence notes that while Jordan was an elite perimeter defender who anchored strong Bulls defenses [[jordan_defense_2240]], his overall needle-moving defensive impact did not match that of a rim-protecting big man, though his defensive plus-minus was strong for a wing [[jordan_defense_3840]].
  * In comparison, LeBron James is evaluated as an elite perimeter defender with exceptional physical attributes and basketball IQ who led high-impact units across multiple teams, even though his total volume of All-Defensive awards is lower [[lebron_defense_0], [lebron_defense_4080], [T2]].
